strongest_angle: Analyze Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes and Bram Stoker's Dracula through literary criticism exploring late nineteenth-century detective fiction, vampirism, and the bohemian symbolism of imperial Britain.

key_facts.fact: In Daniel Cottom's analysis published in ELH in September 2012, Sherlock Holmes and Dracula are examined as representing the origin and end of the nineteenth-century bohemian figure.
In Amanda Fransson's 2019 narratological character study from Linnaeus University, Loren D. Estleman's novel Sherlock Holmes vs. Dracula is analyzed regarding imperialistic representation.
As documented on the Dickinson College British Literature blog, Dr. John Watson compares Sherlock Holmes's deductive powers to witchcraft at the beginning of the first canon story.
In the study on Sherlock Holmes versus Dracula hosted on the DiVA portal, Sherlock Holmes states that nothing exhausts him except inactivity.

quotes.text: You would certainly have been burned, had you lived a few centuries ago
